clue.text: Tore stamps out? He often did

definitions.text: Tore stamps out? He often did

indicators.note: out signals the letters of tore stamps being knocked out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about who used to rip out stamps, answered with a nod to a post office official.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: the letters of TORE STAMPS, shaken 'out', rearrange to the answer, and the clue as a whole describes a post office head who tore stamps from sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a post office would often tear stamps from sheets when selling them over the counter.

clue.text: Messing up sitter chance, my football team

clue.text: Naughty Uncle Rod's a rogue

parts.note: the letters of rod's taken as written, with the S included

clue.text: Praise in text oleaginously

clue.text: Send message electronically mostly rather quaint

clue.text: Lord Chancellor's office cooks law up

explanation.surface: Lawmaking in the Lord Chancellor's office is concocted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooks' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'up' does the work. The Woolsack is the wool-stuffed seat of the Lord Speaker (formerly the Lord Chancellor) in the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: The Woolsack, a seat in the House of Lords, stands by metonymy for the Lord Chancellor's position.

clue.text: Ravel composed a gentle number

explanation.surface: The composer Ravel wrote a soft piece.

explanation.definitionFit: To ravel is to tangle threads together, so it is a synonym of entangle.

clue.text: It's gambled with lone gunman

read literally, a robber with a single arm, an outlaw with one limb

clue.text: Definite caught-and-bowled

explanation.walkthrough: Caught and bowled is a cricket dismissal in which the bowler catches the ball, so both caught and bowled, each meaning out.
explanation.definitionFit: Out-and-out means complete or absolute, so it matches definite in the sense of utter.

clue.text: Russian rebel perhaps, doubly revolutionary and Nationalist

clue.text: Mars location turns out to be …

clue.text: Toff with German name is easy to work out

clue.text: One detective constable in bad mood shows restraint
